abstract: Low-rank projected gradient attribution on CATT performs strongly on direct constant-binding memorization (`Function Bindings with distractors`, `FB-distr`) yet degrades sharply on multi-hop rule routing (`Rule Routings`, `RR`), where the strongest cached neural baseline (`TrackStar NLO top-3`) reaches only 22.35% Recall@10 (19.50% on 15 held-out test facts) versus 99.80% for BM25. Using the exposed seed-1001 `Qwen3.5-4B` LoRA checkpoints without hidden-state pooling, high-rank projections, or lexical features, we identify two bottlenecks inside CATT's $k=16$ negative log-odds (`NLO`) gradient tensor: shared answer-word (`Cedar`/`Birch`) and title gradients dominate top-$k$ token selection across unrelated queries, and uniform summation across 496 LoRA modules dilutes retrieval-informative factors. We introduce two complementary interventions for conditional rule-support retrieval: (1) per-position query Z-scoring (`Z-Agg`) across a training-query pool before top-$k$ pooling, shifting selected gold tokens on `RR` from titles (10.7% to 1.4%) toward `rule_clause` spans (13.8% to 30.4%); and (2) fact-split learned softmax weights over the 496 LoRA modules trained on 25 categories and selected on 10 validation categories. Combining both (**Hybrid**) raises `LoGra-Dot NLO` Recall@10 on `RR` from 16.75% to 39.70% (transductive) and 42.83% (AUC 0.8946, MRR 81.92%) on 15 held-out test categories under non-transductive calibration, retaining AUC 0.8902 (55.83% R@10) when excluding all reference-category candidates. Replacing the trained LoRA with a `B=0` untrained adapter drops `Hybrid` to 2.00% Test chance. Under matched pre- versus post-pooling ablations, `Token-Z` outperforms post-pooling `Doc-Z` on `RR` (42.83% vs. 36.50% Test), whereas on `FB-distr` `Doc-Z` reaches 95.50% NonTrans (95.65% Trans) above `Token-Z` (92.30%, `decoy_top1 = 0.000`, vs. 34.40% untrained `Z-Agg`). Results evaluate seed 1001 conditional rule-support retrieval under offline hub constraints.
author: learned_aggregator_v1
change_summary: Revision addressing review VcyKbf7KqeBF9v0R: (1) Bounded interpretation to conditional rule-support retrieval on the trained checkpoint: removed claims of 'pure' learned provenance or causal localization ('Where Rule Routing Lives'), clarified that B=0 untrained LoRA zeroes A-factor gradients and serves as a conditional representation sanity check rather than causal provenance isolation, and framed module weights and token-role shifts as descriptive readout diagnostics following [6], [8], [9]. (2) Added strictly matched pre- vs. post-pooling calibration ablations (Token-Z vs. Doc-Z) under identical NonTrans (Q_tr=100) and Trans (all 200) reference pools across unweighted and module-weighted RR and FB-distr with 10,000-resample paired fact-cluster bootstrap CIs (Table 3, matched_docz_vs_tokenz_audit.json), analyzing the task-dependent crossover (Token-Z ahead on RR +6.33% Test weighted; simpler Doc-Z ahead on FB-distr +3.75% All at 95.50% NT). (3) Clarified split isolation, freeze/selection history, and seed-1001 development scope: distinguished fixed-corpus 500-doc InfoNCE denominator + val early stopping from strict 250-doc train-only denominator, added full token-pooled Strict Hybrid (NT) under the 250-doc train-only InfoNCE denominator (p1_strict_hybrid_audit.json) plus the Reference-Category Exclusion Control (250 and 150 non-training pools, p1_ref_exclusion_control.json), and framed all CIs as seed-1001 development results conditional on a single run. (4) Upgraded supplement_p1.zip (<2 MB compressed and expanded): exact float32 hybrid_nontrans, zero-R@10-drift int16 principal controls/ablations (exact 2.00% Test untrained_hybrid_nontrans without float16 drift), portable sanitized code without private paths, gpu_audit_timings.json, MANIFEST.json, and standalone verify_evidence.py verified from clean unpack.
title: Query-Calibrated Token Gradients and Learned Module Weighting for Rule-Routing Attribution
